relationships.title: Re: Follow up on USAID LAC planning around RightsCon
relationships.evidence:
On May 3, 2023, at 4:55 PM, Cara Thanassi <[contact omitted]> wrote:
This Message Is From an External Sender
Dear Sandy,
I am writing to follow up on Mileydi's May 1 email regarding RightsCon. As you may be
aware, there will be a robust USG delegation at RightsCon with various events in the
planning stages. In collaboration with the State Department, we in USAID's Latin America
and Caribbean Bureau are organizing a Monday, June 5 event (approximately 9 AM to
1PM) focused on addressing digital repression/promoting digital democracy in Central
America (see description below). This will occur under the broader umbrella of the
interagency Voices initiative focused on protecting, defending, and promoting civic space
in Central America.
The event will include representatives from civil society organizations, independent
media, the private sector, and donors and largely conducted in Spanish. We are currently
finalizing the invitation list, as well as identifying possible panelists. We would be pleased
if one or more representatives from Meta were available to attend (depending upon final
head counts). Moreover, as we work to identify panelists, would there be interest in
someone from Meta possibly serving in that capacity? We welcome your suggestions on
both participants and potential panelists.
We are currently envisioning one panel that includes civil society and media
representatives from the region and another that encompasses donor and private sector
representatives, with no formal decision made as to their compositions yet.
Please let us know if you have any questions and thanks for your consideration.
Best regards,
Cara
Under the U.S. government's interagency Voices initiative to protect, defend and promote
civic space in Central America, USAID and the State Department will hold a June 5
closed-door side event at the RightsCon Summit in Costa Rica. We will take advantage
of the Summit's focus on human rights in the digital age to gather representatives from
civil society organizations, independent media, donors, and the private sector to
understand the challenges, identify gaps and coordinate responses for the promotion of
digital democracy in Central America. This closed-door consultation will center on the
tactics of digital authoritarianism and repression. This includes online surveillance and
censorship; social manipulation and disinformation; internet restrictions; and the targeted
persecution of independent media, human rights defenders, and other advocates and
activists. By bringing together diverse stakeholders, this conversation aims to highlight
local and regional impacts and responses; share lessons learned between sectors and
countries; identify immediate and longer-term priorities, and further coordination and
collaboration for countering digital authoritarianism in the region.
On Mon, May 1, 2023 at 8:26 AM Mileydi Guilarte <[contact omitted]> wrote:
Dear Sandy.
It was a pleasure meeting you as well and discussing ways that we can continue to
work together throughout the hemisphere.
I am copying my colleague Cara to follow up on the RightsCon panel details as well as
my colleague Luis for the trainings we have pending, including the one in Guatemala
and the upcoming election.
